name: Birim REST Lock
author: Melih Birim

sections.description:
WordPress exposes a public REST API at /wp-json/. Anyone can list your users, your installed plugins’ endpoints and your content. Birim REST Lock closes it without breaking your site.

  • Allowlist mode (default): block every route except the ones you list.
  • Blocklist mode: allow every route except the ones you list.
  • Wildcards: /wp/v2/posts* covers /wp/v2/posts and /wp/v2/posts/123.
  • Role rules: apply the same rules to logged-in roles you choose, such as subscribers or customers. Administrators are never blocked.
  • Stop username enumeration: always block /wp/v2/users.
  • Hide what you run: block the route index and namespace listings, and remove REST links from page HTML, the Link header and RSD.
  • Safe defaults: Contact Form 7, WooCommerce block checkout, oEmbed and Jetpack routes are allowed out of the box. CORS preflight (OPTIONS) requests pass through, so token logins keep working.
  • One-click import from Disable REST API: moves your logged-out allowlist and managed roles across.
  • Lightweight: one file, works on PHP 7.4 and up, no tracking, no external requests, no ads.

For developers

  • birim_rest_lock_blocked filter: ( bool $blocked, string $route, WP_REST_Request $request ) to override the decision.
  • birim_rest_lock_message filter: change the error message.
sections.installation:
1. Install from Plugins > Add New, or upload the birim-rest-lock folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Settings > REST Lock to review the routes.
sections.faq:
How do I check it works?

Open https://yoursite.com/wp-json/wp/v2/users in your browser. You should get a 401 error. This happens even while you are logged in: WordPress treats a browser visit to /wp-json/ without a security nonce as logged out. The block editor and admin screens send the nonce, so they keep working.

A plugin stopped working for visitors.

That plugin calls the REST API for logged-out visitors. Settings > REST Lock lists the namespaces on your site. Add the plugin’s namespace (for example /my-plugin/v1) to the allowlist.

Does it block APIs outside /wp-json/?

No. It controls routes registered with the WordPress REST API only.

I’m moving from Disable REST API.

Activate REST Lock and open Settings > REST Lock. Click “Import from Disable REST API”, review the result, then deactivate Disable REST API. The import copies the logged-out allowlist and turns roles you managed there into restricted roles. Per-role route lists are not copied; restricted roles share the logged-out rules.

Will it break the block editor?

No. Administrators are never blocked, and other logged-in users are only restricted if you choose their role. Do not restrict roles that write posts.

How do I report a security issue?

Please email security@birim.one instead of posting in the forum. See https://birimone.pages.dev/security/ for the full policy.
